extracted.intended_audience: postsecondary institution administrators, Title IX coordinators, counsel, and policy implementers responsible for Title IX grievance procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory preamble guidance explaining required standards and permissible options for postsecondary institutions' grievance procedures addressing sex-based harassment, including use of live hearings, written determinations, and appeals. Focused on compliance with final §106.45–106.46 provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional discretion to use live hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: A postsecondary institution may determine whether and under what circumstances to use a live hearing for sex-based harassment complaints involving student complainants or student respondents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department declines to require live hearings in particular circumstances or for certain complaint types; institutions have latitude to structure grievance procedures to ensure equity while accommodating administrative structure, educational community, and applicable law. Institutions may choose to use a live hearing for some but not all complaints, provided they articulate consistent principles and treat parties equitably (see §106.45(b)(8) and §106.45(b)(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to provide a live-questioning process
rubrics_metrics.description: Regardless of whether a live hearing is used, postsecondary institutions must provide a live-questioning process that enables the decisionmaker to assess the credibility of parties and witnesses to the extent credibility is both in dispute and relevant to evaluating one or more allegations of sex-based harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the recipient chooses not to use a live hearing, §106.46(f)(1)(i) allows either the investigator or the decisionmaker to ask questions during individual meetings; if the investigator asks questions, the decisionmaker relies on the investigator's assessment of credibility. The live-questioning process and the options for questioning are discussed in the §106.46(f) preamble discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written grievance procedures must articulate consistent principles for live-hearing use
rubrics_metrics.description: A postsecondary institution's written grievance procedures must articulate consistent principles for how it will determine the types of complaints for which it will use live hearings (e.g., complaints in which both parties are students or complaints with maximum sanctions of suspension or expulsion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A recipient's determination to apply certain procedures to some, but not all, complaints must be made in a manner that treats complainants and respondents equitably consistent with §106.45(b)(1). This supports predictable, non-discriminatory application of live-hearing choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: If a live hearing is used, comply with all §106.46(g) requirements; otherwise follow §106.46(f)(1)(i)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a postsecondary institution chooses to use a live hearing for complaints involving a student, it must comply with all requirements for a live hearing in §106.46(g); conversely, if it chooses not to use a live hearing under §106.46(g), it must follow §106.46(f)(1)(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble explains cross-references and that the procedures in §106.46(f)(1)(ii) apply when a live hearing under §106.46(g) is used. Institutions should consult both provisions to ensure procedural compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Virtual participation and 'separate locations' requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.46(g) permits a postsecondary institution to allow any party to participate in the live hearing virtually as long as the decisionmaker and parties can simultaneously see and hear the party or witness while that party is speaking. The rule requires that upon the request of either party the institution must conduct the live hearing with the parties physically present in separate locations (which can be virtual).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department revised regulatory text by replacing “will” with “must” to clarify the institution's obligation to conduct the live hearing with parties in separate locations upon request. Telephonic testimony without video is not permitted because simultaneous sight and sound are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal opportunity to speak and listen in hybrid hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: When one person testifies in person and another remotely (a hybrid hearing), the postsecondary institution must ensure both parties have equal opportunity to speak and listen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final regulations at §106.45(b)(1) require grievance procedures to treat parties equitably; the Department maintained the position that institutions must ensure parity in hybrid settings. Institutions should implement technical and procedural measures so remote participants are simultaneously seen and heard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on non-disability-based 'other format' communication
rubrics_metrics.description: The phrase allowing parties to 'communicat[e] in another format' was removed; alternative forms of communication (such as typing in a chat) are permitted only when necessary to accommodate a disability under applicable disability laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department clarified its intent that alternative communication methods be limited to disability accommodations; persons who do not require an accommodation or auxiliary aid or service would be required to speak during the hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trauma-informed approach optional, not mandated
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are not required to ensure that hearings and questioning are trauma-informed as a specific regulatory obligation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients that sufficiently train investigators, decisionmakers, and other personnel as required by §106.8(d)(2) will be able to implement procedures that treat complainants and respondents respectfully and fairly. Imposing specific trauma-informed obligations could interfere with recipients' flexibility to tailor training. Recipients may, however, choose to use trauma-informed approaches consistent with the final regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written determination content and purpose (§106.46(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: A written determination must include certain key elements so that parties have a thorough understanding of the investigative process and information considered, and the determination must be adequate for the purpose of an appeal or judicial proceeding reviewing the determination regarding responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department clarified §106.46(h) requires a written explanation of how evidence was evaluated and how any harassment will be disciplined (for postsecondary sex-based harassment cases), and that the decisionmaker's evaluation must address evidence that is 'relevant and not otherwise impermissible' (added wording). The written determination need not identify a violation of the recipient's code of conduct, need not include an express analysis of credibility unless relevant and included under §106.46(h)(1)(iii), and need not specify exact types of sanctions (recipients retain flexibility).

rubrics_metrics.name: Simultaneous notification requirement and its meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must provide the written determination to parties 'simultaneously' (i.e., at the same time).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department interprets 'simultaneously' by its plain meaning ('at the same time') and will not treat de minimis delays (e.g., a few minutes in sending emails) as noncompliance. Simultaneous distribution protects complainant privacy while giving both parties identical copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification about remedies vs. specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.46(h) requires notification whether remedies will be provided, but does not require recipients to provide details about the particular remedies in the written determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To protect complainant privacy and preserve fairness, the written determination states whether remedies will be provided; the Title IX Coordinator is responsible for coordinating provision and implementation of remedies and will communicate separately with the party receiving them to discuss appropriate remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to offer appeals to both parties (§106.46(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: A postsecondary institution must offer both parties an appeal from a determination whether sex-based harassment occurred, and from a recipient's dismissal of a complaint or any allegations therein.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This clarifies potential misinterpretations that only respondents would be entitled to appeals. Offering appeals equally to both parties supports accuracy and confidence in outcomes and is consistent with the Clery Act's requirement for equal appellate rights when disciplinary procedures are available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory bases for which appeals must be offered
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must offer appeals on the bases of: procedural irregularity; new evidence that was not reasonably available at the time of the determination; or Title IX Coordinator, investigator, or decisionmaker bias or conflict of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department selected these three bases because each represents an error that could render the determination inaccurate and leave sex-based harassment unaddressed. Institutions may, at their discretion, offer appeals on additional bases, but any extra bases must be equally available to both parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal decisionmaker independence, freedom from bias, and training
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal decisionmaker must not have taken part in the investigation or dismissal of the complaint, must be free from bias and conflicts of interest, and must be trained to serve impartially (see §106.45(d)(3)(iii), §106.45(b)(2), and §106.8(d)(2)(iii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These safeguards aim to ensure appeals provide an independent review. The final regulations explicitly incorporate the requirement that the appeal decisionmaker review the underlying case independently.

rubrics_metrics.name: No mandatory appeals for simple error or weight-of-evidence challenges (but bias basis may encompass them)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declines to require appeals for 'simple error,' 'clear error,' or 'determination being against the weight of the evidence.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appellate case law does not mandate these bases; however, a determination that is against the weight of the evidence may support an inference of bias, and §106.46(i)(1)(iii) allows appeals on the basis of decisionmaker bias. Thus, parties may raise such concerns as part of a bias claim on appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for 'new evidence' on appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: To support an appeal, 'new evidence' must not have been reasonably available at the time the determination or dismissal was made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This standard guards against parties withholding evidence during investigation to present it only on appeal. The Department declines to treat evidence not presented during the investigation as automatically forfeited because many recipients may not include live hearings and forfeiture could be overly restrictive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability and flexibility for elementary and secondary schools
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.45(g) governs questioning procedures at elementary and secondary schools and does not preclude those schools from choosing to utilize a live hearing; however, §106.46(g) live-hearing procedures apply only to postsecondary institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because parties at elementary and secondary levels are generally not adults, schools retain flexibility to apply live-hearing procedures appropriate to developmental stages (e.g., limiting hearing duration, ensuring assistance during questioning). Postsecondary-specific live-hearing rules do not bind K–12 recipients.
